From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer review of the Seller's update draft and Disclosure Letter

**Framing points**
- The Seller calls these "negotiated positions", but they are Seller proposals. Nothing here is agreed, and our mark-up should say so.
- The Disclosure Letter is helpful to us. At items 2-6 and 10 it admits that Bluefen consent, the Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment and assignment, the bonus funding, the incident scope and title verification are all unresolved. We should use these admissions to support specific protections.
- The figures below are opening proposals with fallbacks, not market facts. Tax periods and on-costs need confirming with our tax advisers.

**Biggest priorities:** SPA-N-014 and 004 (category separation and title), 005 (fraud), 006 and 007 (disclosure and knowledge), and the price and condition items 008-010.

---

## Liability architecture

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) on general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general cap, with title, capacity, tax, fraud and specific indemnities outside it (capped at the price or uncapped).
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 50% (AUD 12m) and accept no lower than about 30-35%. The cap is tolerable only if the categories in SPA-N-014 are separated, because the business is small and a few concentrated risks (Bluefen, data) could exceed AUD 4.8m.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 per-claim de minimis, plus an AUD 250,000 deductible basket (only the excess is recoverable).
- **Buyer wants:** A low de minimis, a tipping (first-dollar) basket, and aggregation of related claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at AUD 10,000 de minimis and an AUD 120,000 tipping basket (0.5%). The Seller's thresholds would swallow most small-company claims, and a deductible basket permanently absorbs AUD 250k of loss.
- Thresholds must not apply to title, tax, fraud or specific indemnities.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion, and any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months for general claims, which covers two audit cycles. Longer, separate periods for tax, title and fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months for general warranties. Delete the "applies to all Claims" language, which would sweep title, tax and fraud into the short period.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Title and capacity warranties share the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Title and capacity claims capped at the full price (or uncapped), with no thresholds, and a long-stop of at least 6 years (NSW contract limitation) or no time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A title defect goes to the root of the deal, and a AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month window would leave us holding a AUD 24m asset with a fraction of the recourse.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** The draft is silent on fraud. Because limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5), they would capture fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out of fraud, fraudulent concealment, dishonesty and wilful misconduct from every cap, threshold, time limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clause. It should extend to fraud by the Seller's officers and agents.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the carve-out as a non-negotiable. The "any nature" wording is an unacceptable attempt to insulate the Seller from its own fraud.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** One undifferentiated regime for all claims, with limits applying "unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for (a) general warranties, (b) title and capacity, (c) tax, (d) IP and data, (e) specific indemnities, and (f) fraud. Each should have its own cap, thresholds and time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure clause 12 into categories. The default must be that limits apply only where expressly stated, which reverses the Seller's drafting.

## Disclosure and knowledge

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure only of specific matters against specific warranties, with fair and sufficient detail. No general disclosure of the data room or public registers.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the data room dump and keep only specific disclosures. Otherwise the warranties are hollow, because anything in a data room could qualify them.
- Specific indemnities should apply regardless of disclosure.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** No knowledge limitation. At most, a narrow carve-out for matters actually known to named deal-team members and fairly disclosed in the specific disclosures.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Constructive knowledge would defeat the warranties and, combined with data room disclosure, would negate our diligence-driven protections. Specific indemnities and price adjustments must operate irrespective of knowledge.

## Deal-specific risks

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours", with the consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter admits no consent or evidence of satisfied conditions exists (about AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue).
- **Buyer wants:** A condition precedent: unconditional written consent under cl 11.2, in a form acceptable to us, with the cl 11.3 conditions satisfied and no adverse terms, and a Buyer termination right if it is not obtained by the long-stop date.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a full CP. The consent should count only if it is unconditional or its conditions are acceptable to us. A "deemed satisfied" mechanic on bare delivery would let a conditional or onerous consent satisfy the CP.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion" for about AUD 3.2m outstanding.
- **Buyer wants:** Debt-free means repayment at Completion. We want a payoff letter, repayment out of the price through the funds flow, and release or discharge of all security (including PPSR registrations) at Completion, with the change-control clause (8.1) dealt with.
- **Recommendation:** Reject a post-Completion release. Require payoff from proceeds at Completion with discharge delivered simultaneously. The Seller's approach leaves us owning a company that is still encumbered.
- Check whether the security includes a charge over the shares, which would also affect SPA-N-015.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses, plus employer on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, to be quantified), treated as Seller transaction costs or debt-like items and deducted from the price, or funded through the funds flow at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company, so we would bear them post-Completion. Cover them with a price deduction plus an indemnity for any amount not covered.
- Also ask whether any further transaction-related payments exist.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate". DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, and DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open.
- **Buyer wants:** Payment by the Seller before Completion, with evidence of cleared funds and a confirmatory IP assignment as a Completion deliverable. A broader specific indemnity should cover title and ownership of the Project Materials, third-party claims, and costs.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity. Make payment and assignment a CP or Completion deliverable, with the indemnity as backup. The risk is that we do not own code or materials we rely on, which is a larger exposure than AUD 180k.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material. The Disclosure Letter itself says access, scope and notification obligations are unestablished (~1,240 records).
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity, outside the cap, thresholds and knowledge and disclosure limits, covering investigation, notification (consider the Privacy Act notifiable data breach scheme), regulatory action, third-party claims and remediation. We also want access to the investigation, Buyer consultation on notifications, and a Seller covenant to preserve evidence.
- **Recommendation:** Require the specific indemnity and information rights, and consider a retention or escrow. The Seller cannot call a matter immaterial while admitting it does not know the scope.
- Ask whether the Seller has taken legal advice on notification.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs". The Disclosure Letter does not say whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Facts first: commitment dates, termination rights and whether any amounts are prepaid or accrued. Then an interim-conduct covenant (no renewals or commitments without our consent). Any pre-Completion commitment that is not ordinary course or not reflected in working capital should be a price adjustment or debt-like item.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the characterisation yet. Request the DD-008 and DD-011 detail, add the covenant, and reserve the right to treat them as debt-like if they are accelerated or bundled to burden the business.

## Title and tax/IP

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the Company's own share register (DD-012). The Disclosure Letter itself says this does not mean the Buyer has verified title.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: ASIC extract, constitution and share transfer history, confirmation of no options, rights or encumbrances (including any Riverlark share security), PPSR search, and the Seller's authority and board approvals. Title warranties should be backed by Completion deliverables (executed transfers, certificates if any).
- **Recommendation:** Treat the register as a starting point only. Complete our own checks before signing and make clean title a CP and a fundamental warranty (see SPA-N-004).

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime". They are not settled; we have not agreed them.
- **Buyer wants:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity and tax warranties, outside the general cap and thresholds, with a longer claim period (about 4-6 years, aligned to the ATO amendment period; to be confirmed by tax advisers). IP ownership and non-infringement warranties should sit in a separate category with a higher cap and a longer period, which matters given the Ironquay issue.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled" and reopen both as separate categories under SPA-N-014. Both risks tend to surface late, so the general 18-month window is not adequate.

---

**Suggested next steps**
1. Send a mark-up that restructures clause 12 into categories, adds the fraud carve-out, and deletes general data room disclosure and the knowledge qualifier.
2. Issue a supplementary DD request on Sandbar, Ironquay payment, bonus on-costs, incident forensics and title searches.
3. Rework the funds flow to include Riverlark payoff and the DD-005 bonuses, and convert Bluefen, Riverlark and Ironquay into conditions or Completion deliverables.

I can draft the mark-up language or a supplementary DD request list if you want either.
